data.article_summary: 本文列出了与YouTube和相关服务的一些重要信息和链接。内容包括关于YouTube的介绍、新闻发布、版权声明、联系方式、创作者相关信息、广告、开发者条款、隐私政策、安全指南、YouTube功能测试以及NFL Sunday Ticket服务的提及。同时，版权归属2025年的Google LLC。文章主要提供了与YouTube平台及其新功能和法律信息相关的资源链接。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件测试的价值、成本和方法

不同观点：
• cloogshicer认为，说“无法测试”实际上是在表达测试的成本高于收益，特别是在需要大规模重构且使系统更难理解的情况下。他不完全认同测试狂热者所说的“更可测试的系统总是更容易理解”，并指出有些情况值得权衡，但需要仔细考虑。
• j_w建议隔离“不可测试”的部分以增加可测试性，通过为不可测试部分编写接口并模拟它们，可以避免这些部分吞噬可测试功能。
• testthetest提到，随着AI的发展，单元测试的成本正在下降，AI工具可以自动生成测试，但同时软件复杂性增加，黑盒端到端测试比单元测试更能提供信心。
• devjab主张运行时断言比测试更好，因为它们在问题发生时处理问题，而不是试图预测潜在的失败。他认为随着解释型语言的流行，这种方法被遗忘，但希望看到更少的“开发者聚焦”的错误处理方式。
• webdevver以讽刺口吻表示客户就是用来测试的。
• diggan认为该讨论内容像是博客垃圾，实际内容在一个YouTube视频中。
• aspenmayer关注的是提交URL的karma分配问题，并提到之前的一个先例，对使用脚本提交内容的处理方式提出质疑。
• somewhereoutth提出一个简化的测试哲学：如果由机器使用的部分可以由机器测试，如果由人使用的部分必须由人测试。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于测试的成本与收益之间的权衡，特别是自动化测试（如单元测试）与手动测试（如端到端测试）的价值。
• 有人提到AI工具在自动生成测试方面的潜力，以及黑盒测试在复杂系统中的重要性。
• 另一个讨论点是关于运行时断言与传统测试方法的对比，以及如何在错误发生时处理问题而不是预测问题。
• 还有对社区karma分配机制的讨论，虽然与主要讨论点不完全相关，但引发了对公平性和透明度的思考。

data.title: The War on the Walkman
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 《The Forgotten War on the Walkman》一文回顾了1979年索尼Walkman面世后引发的争议。虽然Walkman如今被视为1980年代的象征，带来怀旧情感，但其诞生之初却遭遇不少批评。文化评论家认为Walkman加剧了个人主义，导致社会隔离，甚至有人将其比作“感官抑制剂”。批评者还担心Walkman影响驾驶和行人的安全，美国多个州因此立法限制使用头戴式耳机。新泽西州Woodbridge镇甚至禁止步行过街时佩戴Walkman耳机，违者可能面临罚款和监禁。一位抗议该法律的居民Oscar Gross虽有意上诉至最高法院，但在一名耳机佩戴者发生交通事故后放弃。文章提醒人们，新技术往往面临抵制，怀旧情绪常让人忘记曾经的争议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：科技发展对社会互动和人际关系的影响，特别是耳机和移动设备的使用。

不同观点：
• **怀旧与趋势变化**：[wkat4242] 提到从轻便耳机到笨重耳机的趋势转变，并怀念寻呼机时代，认为那时的隐私性更好。
• **人际疏离**：[sevensor] 认为佩戴耳机使人更难与陌生人交流，可能加剧人际疏离。
• **音乐发现与选择**：[comrade1234] 强调流媒体时代音乐发现的多样性，并偏好由人类策划的音乐内容而非算法推荐。
• **科技对注意力的影响**：[MarkusWandel] 指出智能手机和无线耳机的普及导致人们对周围环境和社交互动的忽视。
• **历史对比与道德恐慌**：[xg15] 认为虽然新技术常引发道德恐慌，但其对社会结构的影响需要具体分析，未必与过去相同。
• **适应与生存**：[tempodox] 认为尽管技术变化迅速，人类社会依然适应并生存下来。
• **多功能设备的影响**：[tom89999] 指出手机等多功能设备增加了分心和干扰，影响个人专注力。
• **批判性视角**：[atorodius] 引用历史批判观点，认为耳机和移动设备可能鼓励个人从社会连接中抽离。
• **广告与内容选择**：[relaxing] 认为便携式录音机提供了无广告和用户选择的体验，与算法推荐的内容不同。
• **耳机与公共噪音**：[Lio] 更喜欢戴耳机的人的沉默，而不是公共场合大声播放低质量内容的人。
• **自由的代价**：[gwern] 引用悲剧故事，认为某些自由的代价是不可避免的。
• **历史反思**：[Nifty3929] 提醒人们在关注当前问题时也要反思历史。
• **未来展望**：[jb1991] 认为未来变化可能让当前的技术看起来微不足道。
• **同理心的交易性**：[deadbabe] 批评现代社会中同理心的交易性本质。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及多个历史和现代科技对比，强调技术对社会行为和心理的影响。
• 争议焦点在于科技是否真正导致人际疏离，以及如何平衡个人自由与社会责任。
• 不同用户对音乐发现和内容消费的偏好也反映了技术变化带来的多样性体验。

🗓️  On this day in 1979 the Sony Walkman was first released, marking its 46th anniversary
The Sony Walkman is now an icon of the 1980s, eliciting nostalgia for the ‘good old days’ of owning music, rather than renting it. Affection for the device is now universal, but that wasn’t always the case…
The sudden rise of headphone wearing pedestrians - spurred by Sony’s lightweight headsets (17% the weight of others) - caused unease about an unfamiliar new world quickly coming into view.
Some said it was a sign of a continued rise of Reagan and Thatcher style individualism. Cultural critic Allan Bloom deemed the Walkman
"a nonstop... masturbational fantasy”
in his 1987 book ‘The Closing of the American Mind.’ Neo-Luddite John Zerzan saw the Walkman as part of a modern trend that encouraged a
"protective sort of withdrawal from social connections"
and Thomas Lipscomb, chief of the Center for the Digital Future, equated it with the euphoric drug "soma," from Huxley's Brave New World, creating, as he put it,
"an airtight bubble of sound"
that was nothing but a
"sensory depressant."
In other words it all felt ‘a bit blackmirror’ as one might say today.
(A collection of quotes collected in this 1999 Reason Magazine
article
)
The Walkman, critics claimed, was more than just music to one's ears; it was a tool of societal disconnect and for government officials and law enforcement a danger on the roads, because it limited the hearing of drivers, cyclists and pedestrians.
After a number of accidents involving Walkman headphones, numerous states across the US swiftly put into effect or proposed restrictions, many related to headphone use while driving or cycling. Among them were statutes in California, Florida, Georgia, , Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Virginia, and Washington.
The New Jersey township of Woodbridge went a step further, forbidding not just driving or biking, but even crossing the street while wearing Walkman headphones.
The price for breaking this prohibition? A potential two-week stay in jail and a fine. The law made national and international news, including the BBC who got reactions on the street:
The day the law was put into effect - Oscar Gross - a retiree from a neighbouring town, was spurred into action. Seething, he approached Police Sergeant Lou Monzo, purposefully donned his headphones, and crossed the street.
The outcome of this small act of civil disobedience? Gross became the first person to receive a citation for wearing headphones (even though they weren’t plugged into anything.) Undeterred, he stated in an interview,
"I’m prepared to go to jail for 15 days just to prove a point."
Gross end up being interviewed for national outlets as did members of the Woodbridge town council. However, to his disappointment, Gross was not sent to jail. After the judge imposed a $50 fine, which was later suspended, a frustrated Gross said to a journalist:
"He didn't even give me the opportunity to say that I was willing to serve time in jail."
"No municipality has the right to tell somebody what they can wear." -
Oscar Gross
Oscar Gross was
preparing
to take the case all the way to the supreme court, but backed out after someone was killed crossing the street while wearing headphones. The kind of tragic anecdote that is the inevitable and unavoidable price of freedom.
This chapter in techno-pessimism is a good reminder that nostalgia tends to elicit amnesia about the resistance new technologies once faced. After all, who would have thought the “good old days” could ever have been considered a bad, brave new world?

data.title: Hannah Cairo: 17-year-old teen refutes a math conjecture proposed 40 years ago
data.author: leephillips
data.article_summary: 17岁巴哈马学生Hannah Cairo解决了困扰谐波分析领域数十年的Mizohata-Takeuchi猜想。该猜想于1980年代提出，涉及使用特定类型的波构建形状。Cairo通过构造反例证明该猜想不成立，她利用分形等工具，经过多次失败尝试，最终成功。尽管起初她的教授Ruixiang Zhang对其结果持怀疑态度，但最终她证明了自己的正确性。Cairo对数学充满热情，自学复杂数学书籍，并在加州大学伯克利分校旁听课程。她在埃斯科里亚尔举办的国际谐波分析和偏微分方程大会上分享了她的发现，这是她的首次国际科学之旅。Cairo热爱教学和公开演讲，希望帮助他人并让他们快乐。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一位17岁的研究者Hannah Cairo在数学猜想上的进展引发的讨论，包括对其成就的评价、学术界的反应以及对相关数学问题的探讨。

不同观点：
• [marvinborner] 引用了Hannah Cairo的视频以及Terence Tao的潜在进展，询问社区是否有更多信息。
• [bradly] 认为年轻人尤其在20岁左右做出重大数学发现并不罕见，因为纯数学需要高度的创造力。
• [paulpauper] 强调在任何年龄做出原创数学成果都是极其困难的，尤其是在17岁，因此值得高度赞扬。
• [ablaba] 只是提供了一个相关的链接，没有表达明确观点。
• [ledauphin] 质疑为何一位已经解决了几十年未解难题的人还需要通过攻读博士来证明自己的能力。
• [scythe] 提供了相关论文链接，并分享了自己在研究生阶段学习谐波分析的经历。
• [tomjen3] 从教学角度出发，强调应给予人们机会去超越自我，举例说明了通过布置猜想证明作为作业带来的积极效果。
• [lordnacho] 讨论了历史上数学家如Euler和Newton在他们相对年轻时的重大发现，并比较了他们发现被教授的年龄。
• [chengiz] 批评文章写作不佳，认为应更多关注数学内容而非研究者的年龄，并对提及无关背景（如西班牙学院）表示不满。
• [rendall] 提供了一个存档链接，但没有发表明确观点。
• [waym0re] 对Hannah Cairo的反驳持怀疑态度，特别质疑其在数论论文中使用渐进方法的严谨性。
• [raincom] 预测Princeton数学系会邀请她加入他们的博士项目。
• [Keyframe] 认为原始标题比编辑后的标题更具信息性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：Hannah Cairo的成就及其年龄在学术评价中的相关性。部分评论如[bradly]和[paulpauper]认为年轻成就者值得赞扬，而[chengiz]则批评了文章对年龄的过度关注。
• 对研究成果的怀疑：[waym0re]对研究中的方法严谨性提出质疑，表明社区中对新成果的审慎态度。
• 对学术制度的反思：[ledauphin]对博士学位作为衡量学术成就的必要性提出了质疑。

总体来看，讨论围绕Hannah Cairo的数学成就、年龄对学术贡献的影响以及学术界如何评价年轻天才展开。

Hannah Cairo
was stuck on a math problem. All she could think about during those weeks was a new approach. “After months of trying to prove the result, I managed to understand why it was so difficult. I realized that if I used that information correctly, I might be able to refute the claim. Finally, after several failed attempts, I found a way to construct a counterexample [a case that does not satisfy the studied property and therefore proves it is not universally true].” Ciaro says it required several tools, including fractals, and she had to arrange everything very carefully. “It took me a while to convince
Ruixiang Zhang
[the professor of the course where the problem had been posed] that my proposal was actually correct,” Cairo says.
She was right—and with that, Cairo solved the so-called
Mizohata-Takeuchi conjecture
, a problem first proposed in the 1980s that had kept the harmonic analysis community had been working on for decades. The conjecture was widely believed to be true — if so, it would have automatically validated several other important results in the field — but the community greeted the new development with both enthusiasm and surprise: the author was a 17-year-old who hadn’t yet finished high school.
“When I moved to the U.S. from Nassau [in the Bahamas, where she was born], I entered the educational system as a high school student, although I took classes at UC Berkeley. I wrote to professors, telling them what books I’d read on the subject, and asking if I could attend their classes. Many said yes, including Zhang,” she says. “One day, he proposed proving a special, much simpler case of the conjecture as a homework assignment. As an optional part, he included the original conjecture. And I became obsessed with it,” she adds.
The Mizohata-Takeuchi conjecture falls within the field of harmonic analysis, which attempts to break down functions into simpler components, such as sinusoidal functions. Today, it’s a very active area of research and has become a fundamental tool in numerous applications, from compressing digital audio and video files to designing telecommunications systems.
Harmonic analysis was born in the early 19th century with the work of French mathematician Joseph Fourier on the study of the heat function, a partial differential equation that describes the diffusion of heat in a solid body. His revolutionary idea was to break down this complex function as a sum of sines and cosines. The technique, known as Fourier series, opened the door to a new way of understanding physical and
mathematical phenomena
. “In the theory of harmonic analysis, everything is made up of waves. You can build anything with them, if you use the right number of waves,” says Cairo.
In what’s known as Fourier restriction theory, researchers study what types of objects can be built using only a limited set of waves. “Only certain things can be constructed, and it’s very difficult to understand which ones. The Mizohata-Takeuchi conjecture states that if you use only certain types of waves, you get a shape made of lines,” she explains.
“Once I obtained the first counterexample, I tried to reformulate the entire problem in frequency space. And I observed what my construction looked like this way. Then I realized that, in fact, there was another, much simpler way to design a counterexample,” she states with satisfaction in one of the rooms of the San José Residence in El Escorial, where the 12th International Congress on Harmonic Analysis and Partial Differential Equations was held from June 9 to 13. The event, organized by the
Institute of Mathematical Sciences
(ICMAT) and the Autonomous University of Madrid, is known as the El Escorial Meetings and, in its nearly 50-year history, has become one of the most prestigious in the field.
This was Cairo’s first international scientific trip. “It’s a wonderful experience spending time with other people who love mathematics,” she says. At the conference in El Escorial, she gave one of the program’s scheduled talks. And, far from feeling self-conscious, she enjoyed it. Cairo enjoys public speaking. She loves teaching other students — who are sometimes older than her. Her vocation, she says, is “to help other people, to make them happy.” And, for as long as she can remember, she’s been fascinated by mathematics.
She began reading complicated textbooks on the subject on her own. “I always wanted to be a mathematician, but I didn’t really know what it meant until I learned
abstract algebra
from books. It’s funny, because abstract algebra is the opposite of the mathematics I do now. Actually, at first, I thought I would go into number theory. When I was 13 or 14, I wrote a paper on number theory, but it dealt with a problem that nobody cared about,” she recalls, laughing.

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何开始阅读古英语诗歌，重点推荐了五首非《贝奥武甫》的诗歌。作者科林·戈里指出，许多人只知《贝奥武甫》，而忽略了其他90%的古英语诗歌。实际上，古英语诗歌种类丰富，包括挽歌、谜语、智慧诗和宗教诗，这些作品往往比《贝奥武甫》更易读且短小。文章逐一介绍了各类诗歌的特色，并推荐了代表作，如《马尔登战役》这首英雄诗。作者还提到，古英语诗歌中充满了独特的意象和深刻的思想，值得一读。最后，作者邀请读者参与其主办的“死语言协会”夏季读书会，共同探讨《贝奥武甫》。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于古英语文学作品（如《贝奥武甫》、古英语谜语、托尔金的《旧英语出埃及记》等）的可读性、教学方法、以及是否应重新出版和推广这些作品的讨论。

• WillAdams认为，托尔金的《旧英语出埃及记》虽然作为学术文本出版，但实际上非常易读且有趣。他建议将这些作品集结成套重新出版，但因其非学术身份，申请重新出版时被拒绝。
• EdwardCoffin强调了一篇《纽约时报》文章对古英语的介绍，特别是关于“肯宁”（kennings）的描述，引起了他学习古英语的兴趣。

How to get started with Old English poetry
Five poems to read that aren’t Beowulf
Colin Gorrie
Jul 02, 2025
110
Share this post
Dead Language Society
How to get started with Old English poetry
Copy link

Share
The Shipwreck
(1805), Joseph Mallord William Turner
Most people who know anything at all about Old English poetry will be aware of the existence of
Beowulf
. Perhaps they will even have read it.
1
But far fewer will be aware of the 90% of Old English poetry that is not
Beowulf
.
It’s a shame, because the back catalogue of Old English poetry — the deep cuts — are well worth reading. And, in general, these poems are much easier (and shorter) to read than
Beowulf
.
The entire corpus of surviving poetry written in Old English stretches to about 30,000 lines; around 3000 of which make up the single poem
Beowulf
. But the rest, written somewhere between AD 700 and 1066, is divided among many shorter poems, mainly preserved in four manuscripts,
2
none of which approaches the fame of
Beowulf
.
Ironically, despite its fame,
Beowulf
is probably the hardest poem to start with: it’s long and frequently obscure, requiring a mountain of commentary to explain all of the lore.
3
Furthermore, scholars disagree on pretty much all the big topics about
Beowulf
. When it was written, where it was written, whether it was a product of oral tradition, whether it’s fundamentally Christian or pagan, how much we can trust the seemingly historical material in the poem… is all fiercely fought over. These controversies are worth exploring, in my opinion, but it’s sometimes nice to get started at the shallow end.
Although
Beowulf
is great heroic poetry, the Old English poetic corpus has a lot more to offer than just heroic poetry! It also contains
elegiac poetry
, which are meditations on the fleeting nature of life. It contains
riddles
as well, some of which are quite salacious. There are also
wisdom poems
, which provide the kind of timeless, well, wisdom that you also see in the Biblical books of
Proverbs
and
Ecclesiastes
or the Old Norse
Hávamál
. Finally, there are
religious poems
, which transpose Christian themes into the Germanic worldview.
In each of these genres, there are works that rise to the level of great art that has stood the test of time. They’re just sadly not so well-known today. And I think that’s a shame, because they’re full of surprises: talking objects, epic battlefield speeches, and poetic imagery you’ll find nowhere else in English literature.
I’d like to introduce you to five of them here, one in each genre, each of which you could read in translation in a single sitting. I’ll give you a taste of each poem, why I think it’s special, and how you can read it right now.

The Dead Language Society
. I'm Colin Gorrie, linguist, ancient language teacher, and your guide through the history of the English language and its relatives.
Subscribe for a
free issue
every Wednesday, or
upgrade to support my mission of bringing historical linguistics out of the ivory tower
and receive
two extra Saturday deep-dives
per month.
You’ll also be able to join the
very first Dead Language Society summer book club(!),
where we’ll be reading Beowulf together. We’ll compare translations against the original Old English and explore the historical and cultural context of the poem. Along the way, I’ll explain all the deep lore that most readers miss.
Our first meeting will take place tomorrow,
Thursday, July 3, at 3:30pm Eastern
.

Heroic:
The Battle of Maldon
Battle of Stamford Bridge
(1870), Peter Nicolai Arbo
The
Battle of Maldon
is a near-contemporary account of a battle which took place in AD 991 between the English and Danes (that is, Vikings) near Maldon, a town in Essex.
4
The leader of the English army was a nobleman named Byrhtnoth. The battle was a defeat for the English: Byrhtnoth was killed and, as a result of the loss, the English king Ethelred was obliged to pay tribute to the Danes.
This tribute was the so-called Danegeld, a word still used today for what happens when you pay an extortionist: they come back for more. Or, as Kipling put it, “once you have paid him the Danegeld // You never get rid of the Dane.”
5
The
Battle of Maldon
as we have it today is a fragment: we have 325 lines of what must once have been a longer poem. But those 325 lines are filled with great speeches, heroic deaths, and battle scenes that feel like they came out of an action movie, such as this excerpt:
Ravens circled, screeching for corpses—
The eagle was ravenous for a feast of flesh—
All earth was in endless uproar.
Warriors thrust file-hardened spears
From their hands, grim shafts at guts—
Bows were busy, shields shot with arrows—
Bitter was the battle-rush. Warriors fell
On both sides—youngbloods lay dead.
(108–115, Williamson)

data.title: Building a Mac app with Claude code
data.author: gdudeman
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在2025年发布了一款由AI工具Claude Code几乎全程开发的macOS原生应用——Context，该应用旨在调试MCP服务器。作者有多年Mac软件开发经验，但这次利用Claude Code完成了约20,000行代码中的19,000行。文章详细介绍了使用Claude Code开发的过程，包括工具选择、使用体验及技巧。Claude Code在编写代码方面表现出色，能理解项目代码、设计模式和文档，且特别擅长SwiftUI。尽管AI工具能大幅提升生产力，但仍需人工指导和迭代。作者还探讨了AI在自动化和未来开发环境中的潜力，认为这些工具可以帮助开发者重新启动搁置的 side project。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（如Claude Code）在软件开发中的应用及其对开发者的影响

不同观点：
• pyman：认为LLM赋予了开发者 "超能力"，提升了生产力和创造力，但同时对自身技能被机器替代感到忧虑，尤其担忧对下一代工程师的影响。
• submeta：非常享受使用LLM（如Claude Code）增强的工作流，从代码生成到配置文件修改和代码文档化，都交给LLM处理，并认为这是未来IDE的趋势。
• epohs：LLM对不同水平的开发者有不同影响，可以作为熟练开发者的助手，但不适合作为新手的替代工具，担心新手过度依赖LLM而忽略基础技能的学习。
• benbojangles：喜欢终端和LLM的组合，认为这种简化的工作方式让他从编码者变成了项目领导者，且无需处理团队管理问题。
• simonw：强调LLM减少了开发摩擦，帮助完成最后20%的工作，使得开发者可以更轻松地完成和发布 side projects。
• data-ottawa：分享了使用LLM快速开发小工具的成功经验，如创建显示launchctl任务状态的工具。
• ralfd：对如何使用LLM创建Mac应用感到困惑，显示出对具体操作步骤的求知需求。
• amelius：幽默地预测有人会用LLM复制整个MacOS，并对LLM错误有自我纠正能力表示认可。
• koinedad：发现使用Windsurf和CLI工具自定义工具变得更加容易，认为这是很有趣的时代。
• hadlock：分享了使用LLM工具开发经典Mac应用的实际案例，展示了LLM在复古计算项目中的潜力。
• ModernMech：指出LLM在处理大型项目（如蓝牙功能）时的局限性，认为LLM容易忘记之前的决策，导致建议矛盾，强调开发者仍需具备一定的工程专业知识。
• ninetyninenine：计划让Claude阅读教程来学习新技能，显示出对LLM自学能力的信任。

补充讨论：
• LLM在开发中的角色：从辅助工具到可能替代部分开发工作，引发了对开发者职业未来的讨论。
• LLM对开发者技能的影响：一些开发者认为LLM能帮助新手学习，但也有观点担心新手会因此忽略基础知识。
• LLM在不同项目规模中的表现：在小项目或工具开发中表现出色，但在大型项目中可能出现决策矛盾和上下文丢失的问题。
• 开发工具链的转变：从传统的IDE转向更轻量化的终端和LLM组合，反映了开发者对简化工作流的追求。
• 具体操作指导的需求：一些开发者对如何具体使用LLM创建应用感到困惑，显示出对操作指南和教程的需求。

I Shipped a macOS App Built Entirely by Claude Code
July 1, 2025
19 min read
I recently shipped
Context
, a native macOS app for debugging
MCP
servers. The goal was to build a useful developer tool that feels at home on the platform, powered by Apple's
SwiftUI
framework. I've been building software for the Mac since 2008, but this time was different:
Context was almost 100% built by
Claude Code
1
.
There is still skill and iteration involved in helping Claude build software, but of the 20,000 lines of code in this project, I estimate that I wrote less than 1,000 lines by hand
2
.
This is a long post explaining my journey, how I chose my tools, what those tools are good at and bad at (for now), and how you can leverage them to maximize the quality of your generated code output, especially if you're building a native app like I am.
Copilot to Claude Code
Starting Yet Another Side Project
Claude Code Is Good at Writing Code
Claude Code Is Okay at Swift and Good at SwiftUI
You Can Just Say "Make it More Beautiful"
Context Engineering Is Key
Priming the Agent
Agents Can’t Read Your Mind, They Need Specs
"Ultrathink and Make a Plan"
Set Up Feedback Loops
Claude Code Can Do More Than Write Code
Building High Quality Automation Is (Almost) Free Now
IDEs of the Future Will Look Very Different
I Can Ship Side Projects Again
1. Copilot to Claude Code
My first experience with AI coding tools was when I tried GitHub Copilot, built into VS Code. This was the first tool of its kind, and I was pretty amazed: at the time, it was just autocomplete, but it was surprisingly effective—instead of only autocompleting symbol names or function signatures like a typical editor, it could autocomplete
entire function implementations
based on the context around it. This was a great productivity boost but it still felt like you were doing most of the work.
Then things started to move fast: Cursor
took off
, they added
Agent Mode
, and new competitors like
Windsurf
entered the space. All of the products were leaning into the "agentic" mode of development, where instead of using one-shot LLM responses for autocomplete, an LLM calls various tools in a loop to accomplish more complex tasks: gathering context on your code base, reading web pages and documentation, compiling your program, running tests, iterating on build/test failures, etc.
I had not tried any of these new tools extensively because I wasn't actively working on a side project at the time, but in February 2025, an interesting contender emerged out of nowhere: Claude Code was not a VS Code fork like the others, but was an IDE that was designed to be used entirely in the terminal. It had no traditional code editing capabilities or an overwhelming UI with lots of features: it put the agentic loop front and center. A text box to enter a prompt and not much else. Instead of
augmenting
your IDE with AI, it
replaced
your IDE. I wasn't entirely convinced that this was the ideal UX, but the idea was refreshing enough compared to what already existed that I decided I had to give it a try.
2. Starting Yet Another Side Project
Like many engineers who have demanding day jobs, I have a large graveyard of side projects that never shipped. Building working prototypes is doable, but the last 20% takes so much time and effort that I had not been able to ship a side project for 6 years.
At this point, I was starting to play around with Claude Code and its support for MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers. Anthropic designed MCP as an open standard to allow agents to access tools and other context to accomplish specific tasks. For example, the
Sentry MCP server
exposes tools that allow an agent to fetch issues containing stack traces and other useful debugging context, and even invoke Sentry's own bug fixing agent.
However, the experience of building and testing MCP servers was cumbersome: MCP servers communicate with clients over standard input/output streams, or over HTTP with
Server-Sent Events (SSE)
to give servers the ability to stream responses to clients. It wasn't as simple as invoking a CLI or using
curl
to send requests to a service. There is a first-party tool called
MCP Inspector
that allows developers to test server functionality, but as a long-time macOS & iOS developer, I wanted to try building a native app to solve this problem. I figured it would be a great learning experience to push the boundaries of AI agents, and hoped to come out of it with a useful product.
3. Claude Code Is Good at Writing Code
Let me just start by saying that Claude Code (with the latest Sonnet 4 and Opus 4 models) is
genuinely
good at writing code. It's certainly not a top 1% programmer, but I would say that Claude's outputs are significantly better than those of the average developer. Given a description of the feature you're trying to implement, Claude can:
Locate and read existing source code in your project relevant to the feature
Understand code style and design patterns
Read additional documentation
44481286.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在2025年发布了一款由AI工具Claude Code几乎全程开发的macOS原生应用——Context，该应用旨在调试MCP服务器。作者有多年Mac软件开发经验，但这次利用Claude Code完成了约20,000行代码中的19,000行。文章详细介绍了使用Claude Code开发的过程，包括工具选择、使用体验及技巧。Claude Code在编写代码方面表现出色，能理解项目代码、设计模式和文档，且特别擅长SwiftUI。尽管AI工具能大幅提升生产力，但仍需人工指导和迭代。作者还探讨了AI在自动化和未来开发环境中的潜力，认为这些工具可以帮助开发者重新启动搁置的 side project。

data.title: Opencode: AI coding agent, built for the terminal
data.author: indigodaddy
data.article_summary: 该文章介绍了开源AI编码助手**opencode**，专为终端设计。它支持多种包管理器和操作系统安装，如macOS和Arch Linux。主要特性包括完全开源、不依赖特定供应商（兼容OpenAI、Google等）、专注于终端用户界面（TUI）、以及采用客户端/服务器架构，允许远程控制。开发者需使用Bun和Golang进行本地运行，并可通过修改TypeScript API实现功能扩展。项目鼓励通过GitHub issues讨论新功能，以确保贡献的有效性。此外，文章还对比了opencode与Claude Code的异同，并提供了社区和资源链接。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕终端用户界面（TUI）和AI编码工具的讨论，包括这些工具的功能、使用体验、定价以及与其他工具的对比。

不同观点：
• **反对TUI的观点**：jappgar认为TUI是一种倒退，只对那些对终端有情感依赖的人有吸引力。他认为TUI遮掩了过程和结果，目的是吸引更多人进入编码的付费陷阱。
• **支持TUI的观点**：jeremy_k分享了他使用OpenCode的积极体验，尤其是其反馈循环和自动化测试的能力，这在他使用Zed时无法实现。
• **对TUI持中立/探索态度的观点**：xrd认为TUI与Aider等工具类似，虽然他更喜欢命令行工具，但觉得目前还没有达到最佳状态，并提出是否能有一个通过自然语言控制和修改的编辑器的想法。

补充讨论：
• **关于工具定价和使用的讨论**：brainless询问了不同工具的定价模式，尤其是Claude Code在其订阅模式下的使用限制，并提到API成本问题。
• **开发者的回应**：thdxr作为开发者之一回应了社区的疑问，说明了项目的开发进度和未来计划，包括构建客户端/服务器模型和开发其他前端。
• **对项目和开发者的个人看法**：orliesaurus提到项目创建者喜欢引发网络争论以制造点击量，但同时也承认项目本身是有潜力的。
• **对项目名称和相似项目的关注**：preciz指出OpenCode与另一个项目名称相同，而zombot则提到缺乏配置本地Ollama模型的说明。
• **对工具对比的需求**：jauntywundrkind和adhamsalama都提到希望将OpenCode与Aider进行对比，而cranium则希望对比OpenCode和Claude Code的使用体验和性能。

争议焦点：
• TUI是否是一种进步还是倒退。
• 不同AI编码工具之间的功能和使用体验对比。
• 项目命名的冲突和配置说明的缺乏。

AI coding agent, built for the terminal.
Installation
#
YOLO
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install
|
bash
#
Package managers
npm i -g opencode-ai@latest
#
or bun/pnpm/yarn
brew install sst/tap/opencode
#
macOS
paru -S opencode-bin
#
Arch Linux
Note:
Remove versions older than 0.1.x before installing
Documentation
For more info on how to configure opencode
head over to our docs
.
Contributing
For any new features we'd appreciate it if you could open an issue first to discuss what you'd like to implement. We're pretty responsive there and it'll save you from working on something that we don't end up using. No need to do this for simpler fixes.
Note
: Please talk to us via github issues before spending time working on
a new feature
To run opencode locally you need.
Bun
Golang 1.24.x
And run.
$ bun install
$ bun run packages/opencode/src/index.ts
Development Notes
API Client
: After making changes to the TypeScript API endpoints in
packages/opencode/src/server/server.ts
, you will need the opencode team to generate a new stainless sdk for the clients.
FAQ
How is this different than Claude Code?
It's very similar to Claude Code in terms of capability. Here are the key differences:
100% open source
Not coupled to any provider. Although Anthropic is recommended, opencode can be used with OpenAI, Google or even local models. As models evolve the gaps between them will close and pricing will drop so being provider agnostic is important.
A focus on TUI. opencode is built by neovim users and the creators of
terminal.shop
; we are going to push the limits of what's possible in the terminal.
A client/server architecture. This for example can allow opencode to run on your computer, while you can drive it remotely from a mobile app. Meaning that the TUI frontend is just one of the possible clients.
What's the other repo?
The other confusingly named repo has no relation to this one. You can
read the story behind it here
.

data.title: Lessons from 863 episodes of This American Life
data.author: cryzinger
data.article_summary: 本文作者分享了自己听完所有《This American Life》广播节目的经历，共计863集。作者提到，虽然耗时十年，但听速其实只是节目播出速度的三倍。起初，作者并无听完所有节目的计划，只是将其视为无尽的娱乐资源，直到几年前才意识到有可能听完。作者认为节目兼具高质量和创新性，每集围绕不同主题，故事类型多样，涵盖时事、个人历史、短篇小说、严肃新闻或轻松内容等。节目音乐和制作水准也一直出色，且敢于探讨有争议的话题。尽管是同一节目，但每次都有新鲜感和惊喜，使作者乐此不疲。此外，作者还观察到节目多年来不断精进，故事更具野心，参与人员更多，音乐选择也更丰富。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对《This American Life》 (TAL) 这一播客的多角度评价与讨论

不同观点：
• **正面评价**：
   - **文化与社会记录**：kiernanmcgowan 认为 TAL 是美国文化和社会的真实写照，可能成为未来人类学家和历史学家理解我们时代的重要来源。
   - **创作启发**：willturman 提到 TAL 主持人 Ira Glass 对创意过程的看法启发了他软件创作的思路。
   - **高质量内容**：adamgordonbell 热爱 TAL，并从中学习和借鉴，认为某些剧集能深刻改变听众的想法，同时提到该节目启发了许多其他节目和人才，如 David Sedaris。
   - **独特性和故事讲述**：js2 认为只有 The Moth 能与 TAL 相提并论，二者都以高质量的叙事见长。

• **负面评价**：
   - **内容失去吸引力**：RyJones 提到随着年龄增长，TAL 的内容变得不再有趣，认为 Ira Glass 在20年前就已脱离了“American Life”。
   - **声音问题**：comrade1234 表示尽管 TAL 的内容值得一听，但主持人Ira Glass的声音让他难以持续收听，类似的还有《Hidden Brain》。

• **节目形式与假设性讨论**：
   - **节目形式对比**：TMEHpodcast 提出一个假设性的问题，如果 TAL 是英国节目会怎样，并以幽默的方式描述了英式生活的平淡和谦逊。

• **技术性问题与建议**：
   - **播放速度争议**：teaearlgraycold 强烈反对以高于1倍的速度收听高质量内容，认为这是对内容的不尊重。
   - **技术警告**：xnx 提到网站有 HTTPS 警告。

• **节目内容扩展建议**：
   - **内容多样性不足**：seany 认为 TAL 是他尝试听但难以坚持听完的“最难以忍受的播客”，并建议增加一些关于扩大枪支权利、公共部门工会刑事化、或取消分区法等议题的严肃剧集。

补充讨论：
• **对技术工具的幽默评论**：pimlottc 幽默地提到他庆幸文章没有用 ChatGPT 来分析 TAL 的863集内容。
• **对剧情与现实对比的观察**：disposition2 提到通过回顾《Law & Order》剧情，可以观察到公民自由逐渐被侵蚀的现象，并与现实生活中的经历相对照。

争议焦点：
• **内容吸引力变化**：部分听众认为 TAL 随着时间推移失去了原有的吸引力，尤其是对于老听众来说。
• **播放速度的道德性**：有听众认为以快速播放高质量内容是不合适的，但这一观点并未得到普遍认同。

总结来看，评论围绕 TAL 的内容质量、主持人的声音表现、节目形式以及播放方式等多个方面展开了讨论，正面与负面评价兼有，并包含一些技术性和假设性的讨论。

44482709.article_content:
table of contents
It took me a decade, but now I can finally say it: I’ve listened to every episode of This American Life. Or at least every episode they’ve aired so far, which right now means… all 863 of them.
Anyone who knows me well enough will not be surprised to hear this, lol.
the finish line
#
I don’t think my speed was especially notable. The show itself turns 30 this year, which means my listen-through was only three times faster than if I’d been tuning in since day one.
1
But I didn’t start out with any kind of goal or expectation that I’d ever finish; if anything, I kinda treated the show’s back catalog as a bottomless well of entertainment that I could tap forever, and only realized a few years ago that I might actually reach the end of it. At which point I figured I might as well try.
For those of you who would sneer at my feat, you should know two things: first, that I’m
very
loyal, and second, that I know what I like. But I also think you’re missing out.
the formula
#
There are plenty of high-minded (and truthful) reasons I could give to explain why I love This American Life: those signature stories that manage to be funny and surprising and candid and moving—but “moving” in a non-corny way—all at the same time; the amount of random stuff I’ve learned about far-flung topics over the years, and still remember, and will regularly cite in conversation if you don’t restrain me fast enough; the
music
, obviously. And I very much appreciate the showrunners’ willingness to take principled but not-always-popular stances in their stories, whether it was about
the Iraq War
twenty years ago or
trans teens
today.
2
But I think the show’s secret sauce, the thing that compelled me to listen to 36 consecutive days’ worth of radio programming, comes down to a pretty basic formula:
compelling-ness = quality * novelty
Quality
: Even if you travel way back into the TAL archives like I did, you can expect a consistent level of quality from just about every episode—you’ll get an hour of radio that’s informative or entertaining or (usually) both, with solid production values, and a reasonable expectation that any nonfiction stories you hear have been fact-checked appropriately. And the
music
is always excellent.
Novelty:
At the same time, anyone who’s listened to the show can tell you how it works: each week, of course, they choose a theme, then bring us a variety of stories (or sometimes just one long story) on that theme. Which is a formula, sure, but a formula where novelty is baked into the fabric of it. The weekly theme can be anything from
The Ten Commandments
to
Running After Antelope
to
Embrace the Suck
. There are no recurring segments. And the actual stories span different formats and genres, and come from different producers who have their own distinct styles and specialties, plus sometimes there are guest contributors, and there’s
a ton
of
different
music
throughout
.
Compelling-ness:
Which, when you put those two things together, means you’re all but guaranteed to hear something that’s
new
and
unexpected
, but also
good
. And at least for me and the way I’m wired, that combination is total fucking catnip.
Like, imagine a restaurant that surprises you with a different meal every time you dine there, and it’s usually something you’ve never tried before (or at least a twist on a dish you’re familiar with), and no matter what it is you always like it enough to clean your plate. I would absolutely eat there 800+ times. They’d have a picture of me on their wall shaking hands with the owner.
So even though I listened to 863 episodes of the same show, it’s never really the
same
show. Which is exactly why I love it. Any given episode can include a
current-events story
, or a
personal history
, or a
profile
, or a piece of
short fiction
, or a bit of
serious journalism
, or something
more lighthearted
, or one of those
documentary-ish stories
where they just follow people around and see what kind of drama unfolds, or any
combination
of those. Sometimes
Tig Notaro
is there. The point is that I don’t need to know what I’m getting ahead of time because I trust that I’ll enjoy it, and I inevitably do, and then I get to be surprised and satisfied at the same time.
3
radio time machine
#
One fun thing about following the same show across such a long period was getting to watch (hear?) the progress of its creative arc over time. Especially since I jumped back and forth between new episodes as they popped up in my feed and increasingly old episodes as I crawled through the archives, which made it easy to compare the two. TAL has definitely retained the same core identity all these years, but I don’t think it fell into the trap many long-running projects do where they stagnate or start half-assing it; if anything, the show slowly became a more refined, deliberate version of itself. The stories got more ambitious. They brought more people on board. And they expanded their music catalog enough that they didn’t have to kee
44482709.article_summary: 本文作者分享了自己听完所有《This American Life》广播节目的经历，共计863集。作者提到，虽然耗时十年，但听速其实只是节目播出速度的三倍。起初，作者并无听完所有节目的计划，只是将其视为无尽的娱乐资源，直到几年前才意识到有可能听完。作者认为节目兼具高质量和创新性，每集围绕不同主题，故事类型多样，涵盖时事、个人历史、短篇小说、严肃新闻或轻松内容等。节目音乐和制作水准也一直出色，且敢于探讨有争议的话题。尽管是同一节目，但每次都有新鲜感和惊喜，使作者乐此不疲。此外，作者还观察到节目多年来不断精进，故事更具野心，参与人员更多，音乐选择也更丰富。

data.title: Corrected UTF-8 (2022)
data.author: RGBCube
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了UTF-8编码的一些设计错误，并提出了修正方案，称为"Corrected UTF-8"。这些错误部分源于设计者的失误以及ISO和Unicode内部的政治因素。文章提出了三项主要修改：1. 消除过长编码，确保每个编码都是唯一表示；2. 不编码C1控制字符和Unicode替代字符，避免潜在误解和不必要字符；3. 移除编码上限，恢复最初的UTF-8设计，允许编码高达U+8421109F的字符，并保留未来扩展的可能性。这些修改旨在防止安全漏洞，并确保编码系统的长期适用性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对现有文本编码标准的改进建议及其争议

不同观点：
• Dwedit认为，提出与现有标准不兼容的新编码标准不会获得广泛接受。他以WTF-8为例，指出其解决了特定问题（即表示无效的16位字符），而新提案缺乏实际应用场景。
• maxdamantus提出了WTF-8b方案，利用非法超长编码来处理无效Unicode字符，并希望在保留无效字符的前提下进行扩展。他提供了具体技术细节和个人实践经验。
• josephg主张在新编码标准中强制使用Unicode规范化形式，认为这是解决复杂性和模糊性的必要步骤。
• philipwhiuk质疑剔除某些字符的必要性，并担心新方案会导致现有字符无法表示。
• chowells反对禁止特定字符编码的提议，认为这会增加使用新编码的难度，尤其是在处理文本时。
• eviks对剔除如水平制表符等C0控制字符表示不解，并质疑是否有现代设计系统敢于做出如此激进的改变。
• omoikane认为有意使某些代码点无法编码是不安全的，主张所有代码点都应可编码，即使它们不应被使用。
• duskwuff全面批评了多项提议，包括打破ASCII兼容性、处理UTF-16代理对问题、质疑扩展代码点空间的必要性，以及反对重新引入BOM。
• lifthrasiir提到UCSX作为扩展代码点空间的解决方案，认为其由Unicode贡献者设计，具有权威性。
• oleganza反对使用魔术前缀（如BOM），认为这会破坏兼容性，影响标准的接受度。

• moonshadow565建议设计一种无需大表查询字符类别的编码方案。
• timbray提供了一个相关IETF草案链接，指出该草案列出了不应使用的字符，并认为这是在当前UTF-8限制下的实际解决方案。
• kmeisthax详细讨论了扩展超过U+10FFFF代码点的技术挑战，包括对UTF-16系统的兼容性和处理代理对的复杂性，提出了一种复杂的扩展方案，但同时承认需求很低。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点包括是否应强制使用Unicode规范化形式、是否应剔除某些控制字符、新编码方案的ASCII兼容性及其在实际应用中的可行性。
• 多个评论者提到UTF-16的广泛使用和兼容性问题，认为任何新标准都需要考虑现有系统的过渡和兼容。
• 有评论者提到具体技术如WTF-8、WTF-8b等的应用场景和局限性，以及对编码复杂性的担忧。
• 对未来代码点空间的需求预测和现有编码系统的寿命也是讨论的重要内容。

44456073.article_content:
UTF-8 is decent and all but it contains some design errors, partly
because its original designers just messed up, and partly because of ISO
and Unicode Consortium internal politics. We’re probably going to be
using it forever so it would be good to correct these design errors
before they get any more entrenched than they already have.
Corrected UTF-8 is
almost
the same as UTF-8. We make only
three changes: overlength encodings become
impossible
instead
of just forbidden; the C1 controls and the Unicode
surrogate
characters
are not encoded; and the artifical upper limit on the
code space is removed.
The key words
MUST,
MUST NOT,
REQUIRED,
SHALL,
SHALL NOT,
SHOULD,
SHOULD NOT,
RECOMMENDED,
MAY,
and
OPTIONAL
in this document are
to be interpreted as described in
RFC 2119
.
Eliminating overlength
encodings
The possibility of overlength encodings is the design error in UTF-8
that’s just a plain old mistake. As originally specified, the codepoint
U+002F (SOLIDUS,
/
) could be encoded as the one-byte
sequence
2F
, or the two-byte sequence
C0 AF
,
or the three-byte sequence
E0 80 AF
, etc.
This led to
security holes
and so the specification was revised to say that a
UTF-8 encoder must produce the shortest possible sequence that can
represent a codepoint, and a decoder must reject any byte sequence
that’s longer than it needs to be.
Corrected UTF-8 instead adds offsets to the codepoints encoded by all
sequences of at least two bytes, so that every possible sequence is the
unique
encoding of a single codepoint. For example, a two-byte
sequence, 110xxxxx 10yyyyyy, encodes the codepoint 0000 0xxx xxyy yyyy
plus 160
; therefore,
C0 AF
becomes the unique
encoding of U+00CF (LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DIAERESIS,
Ï
).
Not encoding C1 controls
or surrogates
The C1 control character range (U+0080 through U+009F) is included in
Unicode
primarily
for backward compatibility with ISO/IEC 2022
, an older character
encoding standard in which the
byte
ranges
00
through
1F
and
7F
through
9F
are
reserved for control characters.
It is never appropriate to use the C1 controls in interchangeable
text, as they are very likely to be misinterpreted according to one of
the DOS code pages that defined bytes
80
through
9F
as graphic characters. Corrected UTF-8 skips over them
entirely; this is why the offset for two-byte sequences is 160 rather
than 128. (I would
like
to discard almost all of the C0
controls as well—preserving only U+0000 and U+000A—but that would break
ASCII compatibility, which is a step too far.) If there is a need to
represent U+0080 through U+009F, perhaps for round-tripping historical
documents, they can be mapped to some convenient private-use
codepoints.
Similarly, the only reason the surrogate space (U+D800 through
U+DFFF) exists is to support UTF-16. These codepoints will never appear
in well-formed Unicode text, and the current generation of the UTF spec
actually forbids the three-byte sequences
ED A0 80
through
ED BF BF
to be emitted or accepted at all, rather like the
overlength sequences. In Corrected UTF-8, we skip this range just like
we do for the C1 controls. (This unfortunately does mean that the
three-byte sequences are split into two ranges with two different
offsets.) Again, programs that need to represent actual surrogates
(perhaps for the same reasons that motivated the creation of
WTF-8
) can map them into
private-use space.
Removing the artificial
upper limit
The original design of UTF-8 (as
FSS-UTF,
by Pike and
Thompson; standardized in 1996 by
RFC 2044
) could
encode codepoints up to U+7FFF FFFF. In 2003 the IETF changed the
specification (via
RFC 3629
) to
disallow encoding any codepoint beyond U+10 FFFF. This was purely
because of internal ISO and Unicode Consortium politics; they rejected
the possibility of a future in which codepoints would exist that
UTF-
16
could not represent. UTF-16 is now obsolete, so there is
no longer any reason to stick to this upper limit, and at the present
rate of codepoint allocation, the space below U+10 FFFF will be
exhausted in something like 600 years (less if private-use space is not
reclaimed). Text encodings are forever; the time to avoid running out of
space is now, not 550 years from now.
Corrected UTF-8 reverts to the original definition of four-, five-,
and six-byte sequences from RFC 2044; after taking the offsets into
account, the highest encodable code point is U+8421 109F. The encoding
schema could be extended still further by use of the lead bytes
FE
and
FF
, which RFC 2044 leaves undefined.
FE
would begin a seven-byte sequence, and
FF
would indicate that the unary count of tail bytes extends into the next
byte.
1111 1111 110x xxxx
would be the first
two
bytes of an eight-byte sequence,
1111 1111 1110 xxxx
would
begin a
nine
-byte sequence, and so on; in this way the encoding
schema would not have any upper limit at all.
We are leaving that extension for the future, because the original
rationale for not using bytes
FE
and
FF
(avoiding conflicts wit

data.title: Backlog.md – Markdown‑native Task Manager and Kanban visualizer for any Git repo
data.author: mrlesk
data.article_summary: Backlog.md 是一个用于在 Git 仓库中管理项目协作的工具，通过 Markdown 文件和零配置的命令行界面（CLI）将任何 Git 仓库转变为自包含的项目看板。它支持离线使用，具有 Markdown 原生任务管理、终端内实时看板显示、现代网页界面、AI 助手集成、丰富的查询命令以及跨平台兼容等特点。任务数据以 Markdown 文件形式存储，并可通过 CLI 或网页界面进行管理，支持创建、编辑、归档任务及子任务，且与多个平台兼容。该工具开源，采用 MIT 许可。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一个项目管理工具的实现和使用讨论，涉及AI集成、Git管理、任务分配及工具对比等多个方面。

不同观点：
• **bityard**：对GIF展示效果感到困惑，认为展示速度过快，无法看清细节。
• **nzach**：希望在不将文件提交到Git的情况下试用该项目，尝试将backlog文件夹加入.gitignore，但仍遇到错误提示，期望手动添加文件。
• **cloudking**：提到自己使用的是Task Master工具，未直接评价该项目。
• **urlwolf**：质疑该工具与TaskWarrior的区别，认为两者用例重叠，并批评TaskWarrior的Rust重写版本表现不佳。
• **jwpapi**：介绍如何结合Aider工具使用该项目，特别是通过特定注释让AI参与任务处理，但指出该工具无法创建Pull Request。
• **mrlesk**：分享了自己使用Claude Code的迭代过程和成功经验，并提供自建工具Backlog.md的反馈和代码链接，强调了流程优化的重要性。

补充讨论：
• **jedimastert**：建议修改项目标题以明确其AI工具性质，避免误解为可视化工具。
• **danpalmer**：介绍了自己用Python脚本实现的类似工具，强调无依赖和离线存储的优点。

data.title: AI is coming for agriculture, but farmers aren’t convinced
data.author: lr0
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了澳大利亚农业正面临技术变革，尤其是人工智能（AI）和数字化技术的应用。尽管全球已投入巨资开发如授粉机器人、智能土壤传感器和AI决策系统，但农民对这些技术的看法复杂。作者团队采访了数十位澳大利亚农民，发现他们对技术需求有深刻理解，但同时对科技公司过于理想化的承诺持谨慎态度。农民用“shit in, shit out”来表达对不可靠数据输入的担忧，并希望技术“更多自动化，更少功能”，即简单、可靠、能替代人力的工具。文章还通过农民对Suzuki Sierra Stockman车型的喜爱，强调未来农业技术应简单、可适应、可靠，就像过去的经典农用设备。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：未来农业与技术（尤其是自动化和人工智能）在农业中的应用

不同观点：
• Scoundreller认为，在澳大利亚等劳动力稀缺的地区，机器被创造来填补人力的空缺，暗示技术是为了应对高昂的劳动力成本。
• NoPicklez以Toyota Landcruiser 70系列为例，指出有些机器虽然价格高昂但没有过多的附加功能，胜在可靠耐用。
• bryanlarsen设想AI无人机可以减少对单一作物文化的依赖，转而采用多作物文化，通过小型无人机进行个体植物层面的操作，以替代昂贵的机械化大规模操作。
• euroderf希望有一种智能系统，可以利用传感器和图像数据帮助管理家庭菜园，反映了对自动化园艺管理的需求。
• conradfr指出，农民需要的技术不一定要有很多附加功能，而是能够可靠地减轻他们的工作负担。
• andrewrn分享了在草莓采摘机器人项目中的经验，认为尽管技术有潜力，但许多技术创业公司由于不切实际的期望和技术问题而失败，导致农民对新技术持怀疑态度。
• erikerikson区分了畜牧业与农业的差异，指出其研究主要集中在畜牧业生产者上，暗示农业技术需求可能因领域而异。
• zkmon提到在发展中国家，由于农民缺乏教育和资源，他们依赖化学品和低质量的杂交品种，导致食品质量下降，反映了对技术教育和资源分配的需求。
• frainfreeze以调侃方式表达了对未来农业技术发展方向的关注。
• Scoundreller再次提出，GMO技术初期也遇到过抵制，质疑未来是否会出现“无AI食品”，并将其与有机食品概念联系起来。
• theodric认为，农业自动化并非其主要需求，更需要帮助销售产品，反映出产品流通和市场需求的重要性。
• SideburnsOfDoom以幽默方式指出，农业中“投入”如肥料是预期且有益的，强调了农业中特有的自然循环过程。

补充讨论：
- 自动化和人工智能在农业中的实际应用场景与技术挑战（如草莓采摘机器人）。
- 农民对技术的实际需求与技术公司开发产品之间的差距。
- 农业技术在不同地区和文化背景下的不同需求和应用，尤其是在发展中国家。
- 未来农业技术可能引发的社会与市场反应，如对“无AI食品”的需求。

Australian farms are
at the forefront
of a wave of technological change coming to agriculture. Over the past decade, more than US$200 billion (A$305 billion) has been invested globally into the likes of pollination robots, smart soil sensors and artificial intelligence (AI) systems to help make decisions.
What do the people working the land make of it all? We
interviewed dozens of Australian farmers
about AI and digital technology, and found they had a sophisticated understanding of their own needs and how technology might help – as well as a wariness of tech companies’ utopian promises.
The future of farming
The supposed revolution coming to agriculture goes by several names: “
precision agriculture
”, “
smart farming
”, and “
agriculture 4.0
” are some of the more common ones.
These names all gesture towards a future in which the relationships between humans, computing and nature have been significantly reconfigured. Perhaps remote sensing technology will monitor ever more of a farm system, autonomous vehicles will patrol it, and AI will predict crop growth or cattle weight gain.
But there’s another story to tell about the way technological change happens. It involves people and communities creating their own future, their own sense of important change from the past.
AI, country style
Our research team conducted more than 35 interviews with farmers, specifically livestock producers, from across Australia.
The dominant themes of their responses were captured in two pithy quotes: “shit in, shit out” and “more automation, less features”.
“Shit in, shit out” is an earthier version of the “garbage in, garbage out” adage in computer science. If the data going into a model is unreliable or overly abstract, then the outputs will be shaped by those errors.
This captured a real concern for many farmers. They didn’t feel they could trust new technologies if they didn’t understand what knowledge and information they had been built with.
A different kind of automation
On the other hand, “more automation, less features” is what farmers want: technologies that may not have a lot of bells and whistles, but can reliably take a task off their hands.
Australian farmers have a ready appetite for labour-saving technologies. When human bodies are scarce, as they often are in rural Australia, machines are created to fill the void.
Windmills, wire fences, and even the iconic Australian sheepdog have been a crucial part of the technological narrative of settler colonial farming. These things are not “autonomous” in the same way as computer-powered vehicles and drones, but they offer similar advantages to farmers.
What these classic farm technologies have in common is a simplicity that derives from a clarity of purpose. They are the opposite of the “
everything apps
” that fuel the dreams of many Silicon Valley entrepreneurs.
“More automation, less features” is in this sense a farmer envisaging a digital product that fits with their image of a useful technology: transparent in its operations, and a reliable replacement for or an addition to human labour.
The lesson of the Suzuki Sierra Stockman
When speaking with one farmer about favoured technologies of her lifetime, she mentioned the Suzuki Sierra Stockman. These small, no-frills, four-wheel-drive vehicles became something of an icon on Australian sheep and cattle farms through the 1970s, ‘80s and '90s.
By the 1990s, the Suzuki Sierra Stockman had an iconic status among Australian farmers.
Turbo_J / Flickr
Reflecting on her memories of first using the vehicle, the farmer said:
Once I learnt that I could actually draft cattle out with the Suzuki, that changed everything. You could do exactly what you did on a horse with a vehicle.
It seems unlikely that Suzuki’s engineers in Japan envisaged their little jeep chasing cattle in the paddocks of Central West of NSW. The Suzuki was in a sense remade by farmers who found innovative uses for it.
Future technology must be simple, adaptable and reliable
The combustion engine was a key technological change on farms in the 20th century. Computers may play a similar role

data.title: Intel's Lion Cove P-Core and Gaming Workloads
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary:
Intel的Lion Cove P-Core是其最新的高性能CPU架构，相比前代Raptor Cove，提升了每周期执行指令数，重新设计了执行引擎并增加了一级数据缓存。在标准SPEC CPU2017测试中表现优异，尤其在IPC（每周期指令数）较高的子测试中。尽管在Arrow Lake桌面平台上能效更高且整体优于Raptor Cove，但游戏性能更受关注。

游戏负载的IPC较低，Lion Cove在游戏中的表现受限于前端和后端延迟。通过自顶向下分析发现，后端内存延迟是导致流水线槽利用率低的主要原因，L1.5缓存虽缓解了部分L2压力但命中率一般。尽管大部分L1未命中数据能在核内解决，但访问L3和DRAM的延迟较高，影响了性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Intel处理器的性能表现，尤其是E-Cores和P-Cores的调度问题以及缓存性能对游戏的影响。

不同观点：
• [mort96] 认为在BIOS中关闭E-Cores可能会导致测试结果与实际使用情况不符。他指出，虽然可以理解为了分析P-Cores的微架构而关闭E-Cores，但对消费者来说，购买时更希望看到包含E-Cores和P-Cores调度问题的实际性能结果。他认为现实中的游戏表现会比测试结果差。

Lion Cove is Intel’s latest high performance CPU architecture. Compared to its predecessor, Raptor Cove, Intel’s newest core can sustain more instructions per cycle, reorganizes the execution engine, and adds an extra level to the data cache hierarchy. The list of changes goes on, with tweaks to just about every part of the core pipeline. Lion Cove does well in the standard SPEC CPU2017 benchmark suite, where it posts sizeable gains especially in higher IPC subtests. In the Arrow Lake desktop platform, Lion Cove can often go head-to-head against AMD’s Zen 5, and posts an overall lead over Intel’s prior Raptor Cove while pulling less power. But a lot of enthusiasts are interested in gaming performance, and games have different demands from productivity workloads.
Here, I’ll be running a few games while collecting performance monitoring data. I’m using the Core Ultra 9 285K with DDR5-6000 28-36-36-96, which is the fastest memory I have available. E-Cores are turned off in the BIOS, because setting affinity to P-Cores caused massive stuttering in Call of Duty. In Cyberpunk 2077, I’m using the built-in benchmark at 1080P and medium settings, with upscaling turned off. In Palworld, I’m hanging out near a base, because CPU load tends to be higher with more entities around.
Gaming workloads generally fall at the low end of the IPC range. Lion Cove can sustain eight micro-ops per cycle, which roughly corresponds to eight instructions per cycle because most instructions map to a single micro-op. It posts very high IPC figures in several SPEC CPU2017 tests, with some pushing well past 4 IPC. Games however get nowhere near that, and find company with lower IPC tests that see their performance limited by frontend and backend latency.
Top-Down View
Top-down analysis
characterizes how well an application is utilizing a CPU core’s width, and accounts for why pipeline slots go under-utilized. This is usually done at the rename/allocate stage, because it’s often the narrowest stage in the core’s pipeline, which means throughput lost at that stage can’t be recovered later. To briefly break down the reasons:
Bad Speculation: Slot was utilized, but the core was going down the wrong path. That’s usually due to a branch mispredict.
Frontend Latency: Frontend didn’t deliver any micro-ops to the renamer that cycle
Frontend Bandwidth: The frontend delivered some micro-ops, but not enough to fill all renamer slots (eight on Lion Cove)
Core Bound: The backend couldn’t accept more micro-ops from the frontend, and the instruction blocking retirement isn’t a memory load
Backend Memory Bound: As above, but the instruction blocking retirement is a memory load. Intel only describes the event as “TOPDOWN.MEMORY_BOUND_SLOTS” (event 0xA4, unit mask 0x10), but AMD and others explicitly use the criteria of a memory load blocking retirement for their corresponding metrics. Intel likely does the same.
Retiring: The renamer slot was utilized and the corresponding micro-op was eventually retired (useful work)
Core width is poorly utilized, as implied by the IPC figures above. Backend memory latency accounts for a plurality of lost pipeline slots, though there’s room for improvement in instruction execution latency (core bound) and frontend latency as well. Bad speculation and frontend bandwidth are not major issues.
Backend Memory Access
Lion Cove has a 4-level data caching setup, with the L1 data cache split into two levels. I’ll be calling those L1 and L1.5 for simplicity, because the second level of the L1 lands between the first level and the 3 MB L2 cache in capacity and performance.
Lion Cove’s L1.5 catches a substantial portion of L1 misses, though its hitrate isn’t great in absolute terms. It gives off some RDNA 128 KB L1 vibes, in that it takes some load off the L2 but often has mediocre hitrates. L2 hitrate is 49.88%, 71.87%, and 50.98% in COD, Palworld, and Cyberpunk 2077 respectively. Cumulative hitrate for the L1.5 and L2 comes in at 75.54%, 85.05%, and 85.83% across the three games. Intel’s strategy of using a larger L2 to keep traffic off L3 works to a certain extent, because most L1 misses are serviced without leaving the core.
However, memory accesses that do go to L3 and DRAM are very expensive. Lion Cove can provide an idea of how often each level in the memory hierarchy limits performance. Specifically, performance monitoring events count cycles where no micro-ops were ready to execute, a load was pending from a specified cache level, and no loads missed that level of cache. For example, a cycle would be L3 bound if the core was waiting for data from L3, wasn’t also waiting for data from DRAM, and all pending instructions q

Intel的Lion Cove P-Core是其最新的高性能CPU架构，相比前代Raptor Cove，提升了每周期执行指令数，重新设计了执行引擎并增加了一级数据缓存。在标准SPEC CPU2017测试中表现优异，尤其在IPC（每周期指令数）较高的子测试中。尽管在Arrow Lake桌面平台上能效更高且整体优于Raptor Cove，但游戏性能更受关注。

游戏负载的IPC较低，Lion Cove在游戏中的表现受限于前端和后端延迟。通过自顶向下分析发现，后端内存延迟是导致流水线槽利用率低的主要原因，L1.5缓存虽缓解了部分L2压力但命中率一般。尽管大部分L1未命中数据能在核内解决，但访问L3和DRAM的延迟较高，影响了性能。

data.title: Building the Rust Compiler with GCC
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者尝试使用GCC而不是LLVM来构建Rust编译器的过程，称为"bootstrapping"。该过程分为三个阶段：首先使用基于LLVM的Rust编译器构建初始版本，然后使用GCC重新构建，最后再次构建以验证一致性。作者面临的主要挑战是修复一些导致构建失败的错误，包括处理128位匹配、递归函数的过度内联以及编译器崩溃等问题。作者通过调试技术逐步解决了这些问题，并接近完成第三阶段的构建。文章特别提到，Rust中的`#[inline(always)]`并不保证函数一定会被内联，而只是建议，这在使用GCC构建时会引发问题。最终，作者希望通过这些努力实现基于GCC的Rust编译器构建。

44484363.article_content:
Building the Rust compiler with GCC
Published on 6 Jul 2025
13 - 22 minute read
Bootstrapping Rust with GCC
If you know one thing about me, it is that I love working on the Rust compiler. Some people kayak, travel or play guitar - and I stare at assembly, trying to figure out what I broke.
This summer, I am taking on quite a large task: bootstrapping the Rust compiler using
`cg_gcc`
What does that mean?
"bootstrapping"
is simply a name given to the Rust compiler build process.
So, what I am really trying to do is build a Rust compiler, without using LLVM - and using GCC instead.
The bootstrap process is quite complex, and split into 3 stages.
Stage 1
First, we use a pre-existing, LLVM-based Rust compiler to build
rustc
, and the GCC-based codegen.
Stage 2
Then, we take that GCC-based codegen, and rebuild the Rust compiler using GCC.
Stage 3
As a sanity check, we built the compiler
*again
*, this time using
stage2
.
The idea here is quite simple: if
stage1
and
stage2
produce identical executables, then they behave identically, which means the rust compiler build with GCC is (more or less) equivalent to the one built with LLVM.
Of course, a lot of this is a gross oversimplification, but you should get the gist. Getting to the stage3 is a big milestone - and the goal of my GSoC project.
The 3 little buglets
You may be asking: what is preventing us from building a working stage 3 build right now?
Usually, I would answer this question with something akin to
"If knew what bugs we had, I would have fixed them already"
. However, this is a rare case, where I knew exactly what bugs I needed to fix.
How could I know that?
Via the advanced debugging technique I dubbed
"Giving the compiler a lobotomy"
.
Lobotomizing ferris
Some of the bugs I presented had some pretty clear symptoms:
libgcccjit
(the library we use to interface with GCC) would show errors, complaining about some sort of IR issue.
It would then abort the build, and give me the name of the problematic crate.
Compiling rustix v0.38.44
libgccjit.so: error: : gcc_jit_block_add_assignment: mismatching types: assignment to input_register (type: __int8_t *) from param1 (type: restrict __int32_t  __attribute__((aligned(4))) *)
So, I went into the source code of that crate, found the function responsible, and just patched the problem out.
The compiler does not support 128 bit matches? Cool, a bunch of
if
’s it is.
if val == 0 {
// Do sth
} else if val == 1{
// Do sth else
} else if val == 2{
// Do other thing
}/*...*/
else{
// Do yet another thing
}
Inline causes trouble? Well, out it goes.
/*#[inline(always)]*/ // Who needs inlining, anyways?
The compiler segfaults? It works with optimizations disabled? Well, who cares about speed, let’s build the compiler with none of that "optimization" business.
After axing enough things, I got a pretty good idea about the source of my issues.
I got a stage 2 build working, and was pretty close to stage 3. So, I knew loosely what needed fixing.
Still, I have got to implement those fixes… somehow. Hopefully, they are not too hard.
Go inlinine yourself
The first bug I fought is kind of obvious in hindsight.
It is caused by using the
#[inline(always)]
attribute on a recursive function.
#[inline(always)]
fn fib(n:u32) -> u32{
if n <= 1{return 1}
else{ fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2) }
}
Now, a big chunk of you might be confused as to why this works when using LLVM.
If we read the attribute literally, we are asking
rustc
to "always inline this function". Since fib is recursive, that would mean we have to inline it into itself.
Let us try that!
#[inline(always)]
fn fib(n: u32) ->u32{
if n <= 1 {
return 1;
} else {
(if n - 1 <= 1 {
1
} else {
fib(n - 1 - 1) + fib(n - 1 - 2)
}) + (if n - 2 <= 1 {
1
} else {
fib(n - 2 - 1) + fib(n - 2 - 2)
})
}
}
Uh, you might already see the problem. No matter how many times we inline fib, it will always still contain a non-inlined call to itself.
We are asking the compiler to do something impossible. So, it is no wonder the GCC based backend fails to do this, and errors out.
How on earth does LLVM manage to fully inline fib?
The answer is… it does not.
It was just a hint, bro
Yeap, you hear me right -
#[inline(always)]
does not guarantee our function will always get inlined. Maybe, the more appropriate name would be
#[inline(inline_this_if_u_can_pretty_please)]
.
That might be a bit harder to remember, though ;).
So,
#[inline(always)]
does not always inline. Is this not a compiler bug?
Nope! It is actually intended behaviour, and something
the docs
clearly state:
#[inline(always)]
suggests
that an inline expansion should always be performed
Seems a bit silly, but... ¯\
(ツ)
/¯.
Yeah, so if we tell LLVM to "always inline" something, and it can’t do that, it will just not inline it, and happily chug on.
Sidenote: There exists a way to make LLVM error out in this case, but it is not used by
rustc
here.
If you want this behaviour, you'd have to use the internal
#[rustc_force_inline]
attribute instead.
So, the GCC

data.article_summary: 研究人员开发了一种名为Centaur的人工智能模型，声称可以通过训练Psych-101数据集（包含160个心理学实验的数据）来模拟人类思维，预测人类在自然语言描述的实验中的行为。Centaur基于Meta的Llama语言模型， reportedly 在模拟人类决策方面优于传统认知模型，甚至能应对未包含在训练数据中的修改任务。然而，这一声称面临质疑，批评者认为Centaur并未真正反映人类认知过程，且其能力（如瞬间记忆大量数字）超出人类能力，限制了其广泛应用。尽管存在争议，一些研究者仍对Psych-101数据集和Centaur的潜在科学价值持谨慎乐观态度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在心理学研究中的应用及其是否能准确模拟人类认知的争议

不同观点：
• fwlr：认为使用心理学数据对LLM进行微调是有道理的，但对某些心理学研究者声称该模型能成为人类认知模型表示怀疑。fwlr质疑这些研究者的结论，尤其是通过反应时间和数字记忆测试来评估模型是否能模拟人类认知的方式，认为这些方法可能不合适。

• lewdwig：认为对模型是否准确模拟人类认知持健康的怀疑态度是合理的。lewdwig指出，人们对人类认知本身仍知之甚少，因此对模型能否模拟人类认知的自信断言显得缺乏依据。

• dvh：用《星际迷航》中的角色Data来类比，提出关于模型是否具有感知能力的问题，暗示对模型是否能达到人类认知水平的疑问。

• thih9：提供了一个更早发布的科学文章链接，认为该文章提供了更多信息，并建议更新Hacker News帖子中的链接以指向更权威的信息来源。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于心理学研究者对LLM模型能力的断言是否合理，尤其是当这些断言基于特定的实验测试时。
• fwlr对用反应时间和数字记忆测试来评估LLM表示怀疑，认为这些测试可能不足以证明模型能模拟人类认知。
• lewdwig进一步质疑研究者们的自信来源，指出人类认知本身仍是一个未完全理解的领域。
• thih9的补充提供了一个信息更详尽的科学文章链接，有助于更全面地理解讨论背景。

总体来看，讨论围绕LLM在心理学研究中的应用及其能否模拟人类认知展开，不同参与者对研究者的结论和测试方法提出了不同程度的质疑和补充。

44484994.article_content:
Centaur: A Controversial Leap Towards Simulating Human Cognition
Centaur: A Controversial Leap Towards Simulating Human Cognition
July 3, 2025
Researchers have developed an AI model named Centaur, claiming it can simulate the human mind by training on a data set called Psych-101, which aggregates data from 160 psychology experiments, encompassing over 60,000 participants’ decisions. Originally published in
Nature
, Centaur purportedly predicts human behavior in experiments articulated in natural language. Centaur, trained on Meta’s Llama language model, reportedly outperforms traditional cognitive models in mimicking human decision-making, even extending to modified tasks not included in its training data. This suggests potential for in silico experiment development and new behavioral theories.
However, the claim of Centaur mimicking human cognition faces skepticism. Critics like Blake Richards and Marcel Binz argue it doesn’t genuinely reflect human cognitive processes. Jeffrey Bowers highlights its limitations, noting its ability to recall 256 digits and respond in milliseconds—feats beyond human capability, indicating a lack of faith in its generalizability. Federico Adolfi and others emphasize the dataset’s narrow scope compared to the vastness of human cognition.
Despite criticisms of Centaur, some see value in the Psych-101 dataset for future model testing. Katherine Storrs and others remain cautiously optimistic about Centaur’s potential, acknowledging significant efforts invested that might yield scientific benefits eventually.

click here.

data.title: There's a COMPUTER inside my DS flashcart [video]
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文主要介绍了与YouTube及其相关功能和服务的信息。内容涉及新闻发布、版权、联系方式、创作者信息、广告、开发者条款、隐私政策、安全政策、以及YouTube新功能测试等。此外，文章还提到了NFL Sunday Ticket服务，并标注了版权归属为2025年的Google LLC。文章涵盖了YouTube平台的多方面内容以及其法律和安全相关政策。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Dreamcast记忆卡（VMU）及其功能，与现代设备的比较，以及使用现代技术（如esp32和闪卡）进行复古游戏的挑战。

不同观点：
• **selcuka**：介绍Dreamcast的VMU不仅是记忆卡，还具备8位CPU和单色屏幕，可以作为迷你掌上游戏机。部分Dreamcast游戏允许将迷你游戏“下载”到VMU中，脱离主机独立运行。
• **conradev**：提到使用esp32 SD卡进行类似的复古设备改装，并提供了一个GitHub链接，展示SD-WIFI-PRO项目，表明对现代技术与老式设备结合的兴趣。
• **dottjt**：分享了使用闪卡的实际经验，指出电池消耗大、文件组织困难等问题。具体而言，提到无法将所有文件放在同一个文件夹中，必须按字母分隔，每个文件夹限制约100个文件以避免崩溃。
• **14**：建议将VMU与Apollo计算机进行比较，认为现代设备尽管计算能力更强，但老设备在有限计算能力下实现复杂功能的效率令人惊叹。
• **kazinator**：对类似内容（如“在妊娠测试器上运行Doom”）不再感兴趣，表明对这种复古技术与现代技术结合的讨论有些厌倦。

补充讨论：
• **技术对比与效率**：14提出的老设备效率问题引发了一些对现代计算能力与老设备性能的讨论。
• **实际使用问题**：dottjt分享的实际使用经验突显了在现代设备上运行老游戏或改造老设备时可能遇到的实际问题，如电池消耗和文件管理。
• **资源链接**：conradev提供了实际的资源链接，展示了如何将现代技术应用于复古设备改造，为有兴趣的读者提供了实践参考。

data.title: Swedish Campground (2004)
data.author: CharlesW
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了Mac电脑命令键符号的由来。最初，苹果使用Apple logo作为命令键标识，但史蒂夫·乔布斯认为屏幕上Apple logo过多，要求更换。设计师Susan Kare参考国际符号，选用了瑞典营地标志中的一个花形符号来代替。这个符号在瑞典实际上用于表示历史遗迹或景点，因此不少瑞典用户对此感到困惑。最终，这个符号成为Mac命令键的标志，并一直沿用至今。文章还提到了一些关于该符号的其他来源猜测和相关评论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple使用一个类似于道路标志的符号作为其界面符号，引发了用户对该符号来源和意义的讨论。

不同观点：
• tokai认为Apple选择这个符号很奇怪，可能是一个欠考虑的行为。
• wood_spirit指出，该道路标志在瑞典代表城堡或其他历史景点，而营地使用普通的帐篷符号。
• tauntz补充，该符号也在爱沙尼亚使用，并引用了官方定义，指出该符号表示旅游景点。
• nntwozz提到这个符号也被称为looped square，常用来表示兴趣点。
• JKCalhoun分享了在瑞典拍到的实际道路标志的照片。
• GolDDranks进一步解释，该符号被称为Saint Hannes cross，在瑞典和芬兰用于标记旅游景点。
• mrweasel讨论了符号的同时，还提到了Apple键盘上"control"按钮的标注不一致问题。
• kimmk指出该符号在芬兰也使用，并对Apple使用该符号表示困惑。

补充讨论：
• tmm提出问题，询问Susan Kare使用的“国际符号字典”是什么。
• gnabgib引用了之前相关讨论的链接。
• Duanemclemore和calf则对Susan Kare的设计才能和Mac的历史软件发表了赞赏和回忆。

争议焦点：
• Apple使用该符号是否为欠考虑的行为，以及该符号在不同国家和情境下的具体意义和应用。

Swedish Campground
Author:
Andy Hertzfeld
Date:
August 1983
Characters:
Susan Kare,  Steve Jobs
Topics:
Software Design
Summary:
How we got the unusual symbol used for the menu command key
We thought it was important for the user to be able to invoke every menu command directly from the keyboard, so we added a special key to the keyboard to invoke menu commands, just like our predecessor, Lisa.   We called it the "Apple key"; when pressed in combination with another key, it selected the corresponding menu command.   We displayed a little Apple logo on the right side of every menu item with a keyboard command, to associate the key with the command.
One day, late in the afternoon, Steve Jobs burst into the software fishbowl area in Bandley III, upset about something.   This was not unusual.  I think he had just seen MacDraw for the first time, which had longer menus than our other applications.
"There are too many Apples on the screen! It's ridiculous! We're taking the Apple logo in vain!  We've got to stop doing that!"
After we told him that we had to display the command key symbol with each item that had one, he told us that we better find a different symbol to use instead of the Apple logo, and, because it affected both the manuals and the keyboard hardware, we only had a few days to come up with something else.
It's difficult to come up with a small icon that means "command", and we didn't think of anything right away.  Our bitmap artist Susan Kare had a comprehensive international symbol dictionary and she leafed through it, looking for an appropriate symbol that was distinctive, attractive and had at least something to do with the concept of a menu command.
Finally she came across a floral symbol that was used in Sweden to indicate an interesting feature or attraction in a campground.  She rendered a 16 x 16 bitmap of the little symbol and showed it to the rest of the team, and everybody liked it.  Twenty years later, even in OS X, the Macintosh still has a little bit of a Swedish campground in it.

from Erik Barzeski on January 26, 2004 14:04:35
According to someone from Sweden, on my blog, "that's a Swedish traffic/map symbol used to indicate a historical site."
http://nslog.com/archives/2004/01/25/folklore.php#c005761
from Andy Hertzfeld on January 26, 2004 19:33:34
Lennart Olson, from Sweden writes:
However, I must correct Andy when he explains its meaning here in
Sweden. It does NOT mean campground. Actually, the symbol tries to
picture a castle from above with a tower in each corner. It is
displayed on traffic signs to indicate an historic site.
New Swedish Mac users always get confused why Apple put in a reference
to historic sites on the keyboard... I've gotten that question many
times. Finally I know why! :-)
from Erik K. Veland on January 26, 2004 21:55:03
Ah, so the story behind the command symbol is true. I always thought the symbol was international though, as it's common to see this symbol on roadsigns all over Norway.
Oh, and it's true about it marking a historical site or just "site of interest", not being on a campground.
from Michael Driscoll on January 28, 2004 22:03:23
The Jargon File has an entry for 'feature key' which parallels this anecdote, though it claims the symbol comes from "an early Mac developer who happened to be Swedish".
http://www.catb.org/~esr/jargon/html/F/feature-key.html
from Bjarne Tveskov on February 02, 2004 07:41:28
To sum this up the comments above, the symbol is used to indicate a general "point of interest" in Sweden, Norway and Denmark (and possibly elsewhere in the Nordic countries).

http://tveskov.com
from Alex Rosenberg on April 04, 2004 03:13:13
I've tended to assume that Susan got it from Rudolf Modley's "Handbook of Pictoral Symbols" (ISBN 0-486-23357-X).

In 2002, Sweden introduced four new road signs as alternative to the general "point of interest": a flower for tourist road, a diamond in a circle for world heritage and two signs for tourist attractions and landmarks, illustrated with unique drawings. All four are white on brown background:
http://www.vv.se/aktuellt/pressmed/2002/hkpress17.htm
Just in case Apple today wished to add another modifier key. :)

data.title: Lessons from creating my first text adventure
data.author: kqr
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了文字冒险游戏的制作难度以及作者的亲身经验。作者参加了ParserComp 2025比赛，提交了自己的文字冒险游戏《Lockout》。他指出，尽管与其他类型的游戏相比，文字冒险游戏制作相对简单，但实际仍然具有挑战性。作者前两次尝试因过于 ambitious 而失败，最终通过缩小游戏规模和专注细节完成了《Lockout》。文章还探讨了游戏的范围和细节平衡问题，分为广而简和窄而精两类。现代玩家更偏好细节丰富的游戏，而过于简略的游戏可能会让玩家感到沮丧。作者以《The Plot of the Phantom》为例，展示了广而简风格的游戏体验。总体而言，制作文字冒险游戏需要在广度和细节之间找到合适的平衡。

主要讨论点：文本冒险游戏的体验、技术问题及游戏设计改进建议

不同观点：
• [bdunks] 对文本冒险游戏的积极体验：该评论者对文章和游戏给予积极反馈，表示在阅读文章后尝试了文本冒险游戏，并从中获得乐趣。同时，他们也分享了自己在玩其他推荐游戏（如Suveh Nux）时的良好体验。

• [chrismorgan] 技术问题的反馈与解决方案：该评论者在玩游戏时遇到了技术问题，具体是由于自定义字体加载失败导致的网络错误。他们提出了两种解决方案，包括使用try-catch结构或追加.catch()方法。此外，评论者分享了一种通过用户样式表绕过问题的方法。

• [thrtythreeforty] 对Inform 7学习曲线的批评：该评论者表达了对Inform 7学习难度的不满，认为其语法不透明，学习曲线过高，尽管其外观看起来很有吸引力。

• [ianbicking] 对文本冒险游戏界面改进的建议：该评论者认为可以通过增加界面引导来改善玩家体验，例如通过加粗重要物品、标记出口目的地、使用颜色指示历史记录、简化物品管理和提供快速移动选项等方式来降低游戏的操作难度。

补充讨论：
• 技术问题的普遍性：[chrismorgan]提到的问题虽然是个例，但他们也表示自己在过去五年中首次遇到此类问题，暗示该问题可能较为罕见。

• 游戏设计中的挑战：[ianbicking]指出游戏设计中存在一些挑战，如如何平衡界面引导与游戏谜题之间的关系，例如是否应将确定物品重要性作为谜题的一部分。

争议焦点：
• 文本冒险游戏的学习难度：[thrtythreeforty]认为Inform 7的学习曲线过高，而其他评论者未直接回应此问题，但[ianbicking]的建议部分回应了如何通过设计改进降低学习门槛。

44464536.article_content:
When I write about
the greatness of text adventures
, I pretend they are easy to
make. They are, compared to many other types of games, but it’s still a bit of a
lie. They’re hard to make.
I made one and submitted it to ParserComp 2025, and here’s what I learned.
My first text adventure: Lockout
Since ParserComp voting has opened, the game is now public, and
you can play it
in your browser
. The game itself reveals what it is about as you progress, so I
won’t write too much about it here. You should be able to finish it in 30–60
minutes. Don’t feel bad about needing hints, especially if you’re new to text
adventures.
Lockout
is my third attempt at making a text adventure. The first two failed
because of ambition.
Scope and richness of world modeling
It’s very easy to accidentally try to create too large a text adventure. My
first attempt was way too ambitious, and would have taken months to finish. I
still love the idea for that, but it had to go. I picked another idea that was
much smaller in scope, but it, too, grew too ambitious. I restarted one more
time, from an idea that was even more pared down, and I was actually able to
finish that game. With the minimalistic scope it took maybe fifteen hours of
active work to create most of the game, and then almost as much time again to
fix the 57 problems I received feedback on from beta testers.
1
1
This is a
large time investment for me, which makes it unlikely I’ll create another one
any time soon, even if I’d really like to.
Scope in text adventures is complicated, because there are two dimensions along
which scope can vary: breadth and detail.
A broad game might have many locations, items, and events, but each is
relatively sparsely implemented. Actions get generic responses, and items are
mainly generic scenery without interesting interactions. This is the style of
some of the earliest text adventures; they had to do it that way due to
technical limitations of the time.
A detailed game might have few locations, items, and events, but those that do
exist are modeled in high detail and interact realistically with each other.
Modern development tools afford insane levels of detail, and it’s up to the
author to set a reasonable limit to the detail included.
Lockout
is in the narrow-but-detailed category. Making a broad
and
detailed game takes a huge effort, so for the hobbyist it boils down to finding
the right tradeoff between breadth and detail.
For better or worse, the community encourages detailed games, and among modern
games, a text adventure that is broad and not detailed stands out as lacking in
implementation. A useful comparison to study this difference is
The Plot of the
Phantom
: a newly released game which was designed in the 1980’s, but
implemented using modern tools. It contrasts with
Lockout
in that it is mainly
in the broad-and-sparse camp, as the following interactions illustrate.
CAVE ENTRANCE
You stand at the base of a sandstone cliff, at the mouth of a large cave. Behind
you to the south, a misty Appalachian forest stretches in all directions. A
weathered sign made of pressure-treated lumber and painted in the style of
National Park signage stands to the right of the cave entrance.
The cave entrance is to the north.
Oh, wow, what sort of cave is this?
> look at cave
You can’t see any such thing.
Huh. Well, what can I find in the direction I came from?
> go south
You can’t go that way.
Why not? I suppose what remains is to enter the cave.
> enter cave
You can’t see any such thing.
Oh right, the cave doesn’t exist in the world, only in the description. Maybe I
have to go inside.
> go in
You can’t go that way.
I could have sworn … I guess I’ll go north to enter.
> go north
LARGE CAVERN
You step into a large open space, a cavern created by seeping
groundwater dissolving the sandstone over many decades. The sandy floor is
strewn with rocks and the damp ceiling hangs low, just a foot or two above your
head.
You’re not the first to find this place. Crumpled beer cans and cigarette butts
are everywhere, and the cold, blackend remains of a firepit sit in the cavern
center, and the eastern wall is blanketed with a remarkable amount of
multicolored graffiti.
To the north, a passage disapppears into the rock, while to the west you can see
a hole just barely wide enough to crawl through.
I’m worried about the safety of the ceiling. Can I get more information?
> look
at ceiling
You can’t see any such thing.
That’s odd. Let’s take some stuff we found here before we move on.
> get beer cans and cigarettes
That’s hardly portable.
This goes on for the rest of
The Plot of the Phantom
. There are a lot of things that appear to
exist, but when the player tries to examine them, they aren’t really there, or
they behave in unexpected ways.
Don’t get me wrong! I finished
The Plot of the Phantom
and I had a lot of fun
with it. You can make sparse games fun. However, this sort of sparsity does tend

data.title: Crypto 101 – Introductory course on cryptography (2017)
data.author: pona-a
data.article_summary: 《Crypto 101》是一门免费的加密学入门课程，适合各年龄和技能水平的程序员。课程涵盖从块加密、流加密、哈希函数、消息认证码，到公钥加密、密钥协商协议和签名算法等内容，帮助学习者理解如SSL/TLS等完整系统。课程强调实践，学习者可以通过发现和利用常见的加密漏洞来加深理解，例如伪造管理员cookies、恢复密码或在后门植入随机数生成器。该书无DRM保护，提供PDF、EPUB、Mobi等多种格式，方便在各种设备上阅读。课程源自lvh在2013年PyCon上的演示，并扩展为一本注重破解加密技术的书籍。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：应用密码学资源及其相关讨论

不同观点：
• teleforce 分享了《应用密码学手册》免费下载链接以及多个在线课程和视频资源，重点介绍密码学基础构建模块和实际部署案例，如PKI、TLS、Bluetooth、AWS和Signal等。
• baxtr 提出了对RSA算法在量子计算机面前可能失效的担忧，特别是Shor算法的潜在威胁，并询问当前实现Shor算法的可行性，将其与登月计划类比，暗示其难度虽高但有可能实现。
• z3phyr 认为密码分析学并未被完全攻克，指出如果对密码学家给予足够资助，可能会发现新的算法弱点，甚至在实用的量子计算机出现之前，现有的密码学方案就可能被攻破。

补充讨论：
• mac-monet 推荐了David Wong的《Real World Cryptography》一书，认为对密码学感兴趣的人值得一读。
• xavdid 补充了另一个实用资源链接（cryptopals.com），该网站提供许多密码学理论的实际案例。
• anorphirith 简单表达了对这类密码学资源的喜爱。
• physix 对《应用密码学手册》的内容质量表示赞赏，并表示有继续阅读的兴趣。
• pythops 感谢资源分享并表示赞赏。

争议焦点：
• baxtr 和 z3phyr 对密码学未来安全性的看法存在潜在争议。baxtr 担心量子计算机和Shor算法的实现可能使RSA失效，而 z3phyr 则认为即便没有实用量子计算机，现有的密码学也可能因新的数学发现而被攻破。

整体来看，讨论围绕密码学资源分享及其安全性展开，涉及量子计算对传统密码学的潜在威胁和当前密码学的未解问题。

44484074.article_content:
Crypto
101
Crypto 101 is an introductory course on cryptography,
freely available for programmers of all ages and skill
levels.
Get current version (PDF)
Tweet
Start to finish.
Comes with everything you need to understand complete
systems such as SSL/TLS: block ciphers, stream ciphers,
hash functions, message authentication codes, public key
encryption, key agreement protocols, and signature
algorithms.
Learn by doing.
Learn how to exploit common cryptographic flaws, armed
with nothing but a little time and your favorite
programming language.
Forge administrator cookies, recover passwords, and even
backdoor your own random number generator.
Works everywhere.
DRM-free and available in all common formats:
PDF (for Mac and PC)
EPUB (for most ebook readers, iPad and iPhone)
Mobi (for Kindle)
Crypto 101: the presentation
Crypto 101 started as a presentation at PyCon 2013. It
tries to go through all of the major dramatis personae of
cryptography to make TLS work in 45 minutes. This book is
the natural extension of that, with an extensive focus on
breaking cryptography.
Made with love
by
lvh
.

data.title: Why English doesn't use accents
data.author: sandbach
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了为什么英语不使用音标符号（如é, à, ç等），而法语却广泛使用。故事通过一位虚构的僧侣戈德温在诺曼征服后的经历，展示了英语在诺曼征服后受到法语的影响。诺曼人带来的古法语并没有使用音标符号，这影响了英语的书写方式。尽管现代法语使用多种音标符号，但古法语在征服时期并没有这些特征。因此，英语在演变过程中也不采用音标符号。文章还提到，诺曼征服后，法语在英格兰的统治地位虽是暂时的，但其对英语的词汇、发音和拼写产生了深远影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英语是否应使用变音符号（diacritics）以及英语的演变和标准化问题

不同观点：
• [r00f] 强烈反对认为英语不使用变音符号是“ shame” 的看法。作为第二语言使用者，他更喜欢英语的“干净”书写形式，并认为法语中过多的书写标记令人困惑。
• [LurkandComment] 认为英语是不断演变的，其规则在很大程度上是由出版商、广播公司和教育机构等外部力量标准化的。英语的灵活性很高，规则有时是任意且特定于某些需求的。
• [amelius] 指出英语不使用重音符号是因为使用者不在乎拼写和发音的对应关系，并引用了“Ghoti”这个例子来说明英语拼写的不规则性。
• [KurSix] 认为评论开头引用Godwin是一个 clever 的做法，并指出英语避免使用变音符号实际上是对法语影响的讽刺。
• [mikequinlan] 和 [meindnoch] 都幽默地提到早期抄写员可能是为了适应7位ASCII码而减少字符数量。
• [eahm] 通过描述意大利多种方言和口音的存在，表明其他语言（如意大利语）也有复杂的语音和书写系统。
• [porphyra] 和 [OJFord] 提到英语中仍然存在一些使用变音符号的情况，如“coöperate”和“réelect”，尽管这种用法越来越少见。
• [dvh] 以幽默的方式表达了对英语引入变音符号可能导致拼写竞赛结束的担忧。
• [nelox] 认为声称“英语不使用重音”是天真的，指出英语中存在许多带重音的外来词，如“café”和“crème brûlée”。
• [Dwedit] 指出变音符号的使用并不总是明确的，不同语言有不同的惯例，例如“ā”在不同语言中可能代表不同的声音。
• [richrichardsson] 批评英语中组合字母如“sh”, “th”, “ee”, “oo”, “ou”等的发音不规则性，并与克罗地亚语对比，后者发音更规则。
• [andy99] 提出一个理论，认为英语的流行是因为其发音编码的信息量较少，使得即使有口音也能被理解，这有助于其作为通用语言的地位。

补充讨论：
- 英语规则的灵活性与标准化的矛盾。
- 不同语言在书写与发音对应关系上的差异。
- 变音符号在现代英语中的使用频率和其逐渐减少的趋势。
- 英语作为通用语言的独特优势，包括其对非母语者的包容性。
- 英语拼写与发音不规则性的具体例子及其对学习者的挑战。

Canterbury, AD 1105
The cold of the stone floor in the scriptorium creeps up through Godwin’s boots. He pays it no mind. Before him lies a copy of the
Chronicle,
just arrived from the old capital of Winchester. In it is written the history of the English people. His people.
Today, his job is to make another copy. No difficult task for Godwin, or any monk.
But Abbot Robert will want to inspect the work before vespers. Abbot Robert. A Norman. Last week, the abbot pointed at Godwin’s lettering and called it “crude.” The word still stings.
Godwin’s quill forms the letters
scip
. The passage is about a foul fleet of ships: the raiding parties of Danes that had harried the coast, whom the great King Alfred eventually brought to heel. If only England had a king like that today.
Godwin stares at the word.
Scip
. It’s the right word, the right spelling. The ‘sc’ makes the same sound that the Normans spell ‘sh.’ But Robert won’t see it that way. For him, this will be nothing but Saxon stubbornness.
Godwin takes up his knife. The steel edge scrapes away the ink, taking a thin layer of the vellum with it. He smooths the spot and writes the word again, this time as he knows Robert will want it:
ship
. An English word, somehow made foreign.
He works on, his hand steady. He reaches a later entry: the arrival of a new queen. Pride or the devil takes hold of his soul, and he writes
cwen
. He thinks with a smile of Edith, the last English queen, a woman of his grandfather's time.
Then the smile vanishes. There are no more English queens or kings. Only Normans.
He scrapes the vellum clean again and writes it like a Norman would:
queen
. He writes the ‘e’ twice so the Normans know to drag out the sound. The ink settles, black and final.
He looks at the two words.
Ship. Queen.
This is writing that even a Norman abbot will find acceptable. Good work, he’ll surely say. But Godwin isn’t so sure. He dips his quill again into the ink and continues to rewrite the past.

Our fictional monk Godwin lived in the wake of the single most significant event in the history of the English language: the Norman Conquest of 1066.
Before the Conquest, English — albeit an old form of English — was the language of power and government in England. After the Conquest, French took its place for centuries.
It was but a temporary replacement: English eventually re-established itself in the halls of power, thanks to the gradual loss of English territory in France and the birth of a new English identity during the Renaissance. But the period of French dominance left its mark on all aspects of the language, from vocabulary to pronunciation. And, as Godwin found to his chagrin, it had a revolutionary impact on English spelling.

44484137.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了为什么英语不使用音标符号（如é, à, ç等），而法语却广泛使用。故事通过一位虚构的僧侣戈德温在诺曼征服后的经历，展示了英语在诺曼征服后受到法语的影响。诺曼人带来的古法语并没有使用音标符号，这影响了英语的书写方式。尽管现代法语使用多种音标符号，但古法语在征服时期并没有这些特征。因此，英语在演变过程中也不采用音标符号。文章还提到，诺曼征服后，法语在英格兰的统治地位虽是暂时的，但其对英语的词汇、发音和拼写产生了深远影响。
